sentences.text: The genus Protodontopteryx contains only one known species, Protodontopteryx ruthae.
This bird possessed an estimated wingspan of about 1 meter, making it roughly the size of an average gull.
Its beak was deeper at the base and tapered more strongly toward the tip compared to other pelagornithids.
External nostrils were larger and more similar to those of albatrosses than the reduced nostrils found in later pelagornithids.
The species name honors Ruth Love, the wife of the collector Leigh Love.
Researchers suggest Protodontopteryx was less pelagic than later relatives, as its larger nostrils were likely less adapted for saltwater immersion.
The holotype specimen was collected in New Zealand's Canterbury Region on November 11, 2017, by fossil hunter Leigh Love.
The species was formally described in 2019 by a team including Gerald Mayr, Vanesa L. De Pietri, Leigh Love, Al Mannering, and Richard Paul Scofield.
Researchers suggest Protodontopteryx may have been mainly piscivorous, whereas later species likely foraged for squid and molluscs.
Protodontopteryx belongs to the family Pelagornithidae.
During the early Paleocene, New Zealand had a tropical climate with sea temperatures of about 25 degrees Celsius.
The time range for Protodontopteryx is estimated between 61.66 and 59.24 million years ago.
